subject: Mid-contract capacity top-up and co-term options
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@orbithealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: OrbitHealth Procurement <procurement@orbithealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract capacity bump — options and impact

Hi Hannah,

Hope you’re well. We’re seeing a faster-than-expected uptake on our new charting feature and estimate we’ll need an additional 30% capacity for the rest of the contract year (roughly Sep–Dec).

Can you outline the billing/pricing impact for a mid-contract top-up? Specifically: 1) pro-rata or monthly billing options, 2) impact on our existing discount tier, and 3) whether we can co-term the top-up to our Jan 31 renewal date. Procurement would like a ballpark (monthly burn + one-time setup) so we can review internally.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
VP Product, OrbitHealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity bump — options and impact

Hi Samira — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the traction here. I pulled together a short set of scenarios and included billing/proration examples in the attached workbook (Redwood_Uplift_Scenarios_v2.xlsx). High-level: 

- Billing models: monthly add-on (charged monthly at list rate, pro-rated first month) OR one-time uplift purchase that we amortize over remaining term (appears as a single invoice + credits applied monthly)
- Discount impact: because you’re already in our 18% committed tier, the standard approach is to keep your effective discount for the existing commit and apply a slightly lower uplift discount for midterm top-ups (we typically offer 5–8% off list on top-ups depending on uplift size).
- Co-terming: we can co-term to Jan 31. That requires either (A) an amendment that annualizes the top-up into your current commit or (B) a separate top-up that expires on co-term date (short-term bucket). Option A reduces unit price but requires signature and a short amendment.

Irene — can you confirm the invoicing language and how we’d reflect the amortized option in our billing system? Ben — I called out two suggested uplift bands in the workbook; would you be comfortable sharing one preferred band for OrbitHealth so I can prepare a formal amendment?

Attachments: Redwood_Uplift_Scenarios_v2.xlsx (Excel workbook with cost scenarios and monthly run-rate),

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@orbithealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity bump — options and impact

Thanks Hannah — reviewed the scenarios. Samira, quick note from pricing side: given the 30% uplift ask and the size of OrbitHealth’s existing commit, I’d propose the following pragmatic offer to expedite procurement: 

- Band A (preferred): 30% uplift added as an annualized amendment to co-term on Jan 31 — unit price = existing committed rate less a 6% uplift discount. One-time amendment + monthly billing shows reduced unit economics and keeps your committed tier intact.
- Band B (fast path): Short-term top-up bucket through Jan 31 — 30% at list less a 3% uplift discount, invoiced monthly, no amendment signature other than order confirmation.

If Procurement needs PO-first, Band B is the path to get you live quickly while we process the amendment for Band A. If you want the math spelled out in the email I’ll paste a quick table; otherwise I’ll include exact numbers in the amendment draft.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@orbithealth.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity bump — options and impact

Looping in quick operational notes so Procurement has clarity: 

- Pro-rata mechanics: first partial-month charge = list-rate * (days remaining / days in month) * uplift quantity. Subsequent months bill at agreed uplift unit price.
- Amortized amendment (Band A): we generate an amendment that increases the committed quantity and adjusts the committed unit price; revenue recognition will show a one-time amendment invoice if you choose to prepay, or we can amortize internally for reporting while still invoicing monthly.
- Co-term paperwork: standard amendment + signature. Typical turnaround for legal review at OrbitHealth size is 3–7 business days.
- Attachments: I’m attaching the SOW draft with our redlines for scope impact and integration (SOW_draft_redlines.pdf). Please confirm whether OrbitHealth procurement needs a PO number on the amendment or whether a DocuSign signature is sufficient.

Irene Choi
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOW_draft_redlines.pdf (redlines called out on pages 2–3)

From: Samira Khan <samira@orbithealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity bump — options and impact

Team — thank you, this is helpful and aligns with what procurement asked for. We’re going to take Band B (fast path) to get capacity in place immediately and submit a PO this week so we can get started Sep 1. In parallel, we’ll sign Band A amendment to annualize the uplift and secure the improved rate. Please: 

1) Send me the Band B order confirmation (PO-friendly invoice line items) so procurement can cut the PO.
2) Send the Band A amendment draft for signature — we’ll route internally once legal gives a quick thumbs-up.
3) Confirm any lead time needed for the capacity to appear on your side (we may need the seats available by Sep 1).

I’m attaching the PO as a placeholder (OrbitHealth_PO_20260829.pdf). We’ll follow up with the signed amendment once received.

Best,
Samira
